paragraphs.text: Muhammad Ali Mazhar, J: All aforesaid Civil Petitions for leave to appeal are directed against the consolidated judgment CPLA.No.3933/2025,etc -2- dated 22.05.2025 passed by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Medical Teaching Institutions Appellate Tribunal (Tribunal) in Medical Teaching Institutions (MTIs) Appeal.No.49/2024 & Appeal No.47/2024.

Nonetheless, out of four Civil Petitions against one and the same impugned judgment, Civil Petition No.3933/2025, 9022- P/2024 and 923-P/2025 are time barred but certain satisfactory reasons have been shown in the applications for condonation and there is no opposition for condoning the delay from other side, therefore in the interest of justice, the delay is condoned and C.M.A No.7160/2025, 1275-P/2025 and 1276- P/2025 moved for condonation of delay are disposed of accordingly and all civil petitions heard together.

The short and snappy facts of the case are that the petitioner in CP.3933/25 (Policy Board) is a statutory body established under Section 4 of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Medical Teaching Institutions Reforms Act, 2015 (MTI Act), vested in the various powers inter alia the recommendations of model regulations, policies and amendments pursuant to Section 4A (4)(d) of the MTI Act. The Policy Board in January 2023 approved certain amendments to the Appendix-8 of the Model MTI Regulations and also incorporated a clause for "Accelerated Promotion for Outstanding Merit" which allowed promotion after a minimum period of 4 years of service, subject to achieving a score of 70% or more. The policy was meant to encourage the faculty members to be equipped with latest knowledge and research. The recommendations were circulated vide Office Order dated 22.02.2023 for adoption of amended policy by the respective Boards of Governors (BoG). As a consequence of amended policy, Dr. Yasir Rehman Khattak, petitioner in CPLA.922- P/25 and Dr. Nasreen Kishwar, petitioner in CPLA.923-P/25 both applied for promotion under clause (c) of amended Appendix-8 for accelerated promotion to post of Associate Professor. The Departmental Promotion Committee (DPC) CPLA.No.3933/2025,etc -3- evaluated their case and found them fit under the accelerated promotion criteria. When the matter was forwarded to the Institutional Promotion Committee (IPC) for further evaluation, they declared aforesaid persons ineligible due to lacking five years’ experience as a minimum prerequisite under the PM&DC Regulations. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied, Dr.Yasir Rahman filed Appeal No.49/2024 with the prayer for setting aside the decision of declaring him ineligible for accelerated promotion being ultra vires the MTI Act and Regulations and also sought directions against the respondents to grant him promotion to the post of Associate Professor. Whereas Dr. Nasreen Kishwar also filed the Appeal No 47/2024 with more or less the identical prayers and she also sought directions against the respondents to promote her as Associate Professor in accordance with the MTI Promotion Regulations (2021) as well as the recommendations of the DPC. However, not only were both the aforesaid appeals dismissed by the learned Tribunal but some weird directions were also issued beyond the scope of pleadings, therefore not only the original appellants but the Policy Board and Lady Reading Hospital through its BOG also challenged the same impugned judgment on various grounds.

The learned counsel for the petitioners argued that the jurisdiction of learned Tribunal was invoked by Dr. Yasir Rehman Khattak and Dr. Nasreen Kishwar to decide whether the promotions were rightly denied to them despite approval of DPC but the learned Tribunal passed certain directions in concluding paragraphs No. 2, 3, 4, and 5 of the impugned judgment against the Policy Board without providing any opportunity of hearing to them. All such directions amount to usurp the executive and administrative powers and functions of the BoGs and the Policy Board. No opportunity of hearing was provided to the Policy Board before passing adverse directions against them. It was further contended that the CPLA.No.3933/2025,etc -4- powers of Policy Board have been misinterpreted by the learned Tribunal such as the said powers are limited to recommendation without any authority to amend model regulations, and the Tribunal also failed to appreciate that the act of recommending amendments to model regulations is a fundamental part of statutory function of Policy Board to ensure uniformity and consistency in the policies across all MTIS. It was further averred that the learned Tribunal has committed jurisdictional error by venturing into the domain of policy making and administration in exercise of suo moto jurisdiction not permissible under the law.

The learned counsel for the respondents argued that the learned Tribunal traveled beyond the scope of its appellate jurisdiction and erred in law by rendering declarations and specific directions, particularly in concluding paragraphs of the impugned judgment. It was further contended that learned Tribunal does not have any suo moto powers and it acted without lawful authority. The directions issued for scrutinizing and reversion of all promotions across all MTIs since 2015, is not only harsh but as a matter of fact, such relief was neither sought by the appellants before the learned Tribunal nor any such claim or prayer was the subject matter of appeals. The findings rendered by the learned Tribunal created serious administrative calamity. The directions of reverting all employees promoted since 2015 without making them party or without issuing any notice to them for providing the right of audience was illegal which seriously affected countless individuals.

In sync, the learned Additional Advocate General, KPK also supported the contention raised by the counsel appearing for KGMC/HMC Peshawar and argued that the learned Tribunal acted beyond its jurisdiction. Whilst dismissing the appeals of Dr. Yasir Rehman Khattak and Dr. Nasreen Kishwar, it exercised suo moto powers not vested in it under the law that CPLA.No.3933/2025,etc -5- created administrative crises in the MTIs. The order of the scrutiny and reversion of all promotions across all MTIs since 2015 was passed even without issuing notice to the affectees which blatantly violated the right to fair trial and due process.

Heard the arguments. The rationale of promulgating MTI Act was to provide autonomy to the Government owned Medical Teaching Institutions and their affiliated teaching hospitals in the Province of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to improve performance, enhance effectiveness, efficiency and responsiveness for the provision of quality healthcare services to the people of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and to regulate on sound physical and technical footings the service being rendered by said institutions and other matters ancillary and incidental thereto. According to Section 2 (i) (definition clause), “Medical Teaching Institution” (MTI) means, a medical college, a dental college or other health related teaching institutions and their affiliated teaching hospitals in the public sector; or any public sector teaching hospital which is affiliated with or attached to a medical college, a dental college or any other health related teaching institution of private sector or of any autonomous institution of public sector; or a specialized care hospital in the public sector notified as such by the Health Department of Government, providing healthcare services, medical education, medical training or medical research, as the case may be, and the setting up of each of the above referred institutions is funded in majority by public funds or the majority operating expenses of which are financed from public funds; or directly under the control of Government.

In harmony with Section 4A of the MTI Act, the policy board is constituted by the Government of KPK on the recommendations of Search and Nomination Council at Provincial level to determine in consultation with Government, the standards for the MTIs and its enhancement from time to time, as and when required; recommend to Government CPLA.No.3933/2025,etc -6- policies for the improvement of the Medical Teaching Institutions; recommend to Government various rules and amendments therein that it may seek to make; recommend model regulations and other policies and amendments therein, to be framed by the Board of each Medical Teaching Institution; plan and implement specialized central training programs as and when required for management and employees of all Medical Teaching Institutions; establish the minimum qualification standard, for all posts in Medical Teaching Institutions to ensure merit base appointment; provided that the Board of any Medical Teaching Institution may enhance such minimum qualification of merit at their discretion; provide guidance and advice on any matter referred by the Board or Government; review the annual reports of each Medical Teaching Institution and give recommendations thereon; and assist, aid or advise the Government on any matter relating to the health sector as referred to them by the Government.

Whereas Section 5 of the MTI Act relates to the BOG for each MTI to administer and manage its affairs and shall have overall superintendence and control over the functions and all matters of a MTI. However under sub-section (7), it is provided that any member of the Board, who has been removed prior to completion of his term of three (03) years, may file an appeal in the Appellate Tribunal against the decision of his removal. While Section 16 is germane to service of the Medical Teaching Institution, whereby the Board may appoint such persons, experts or consultants in the service of a MTI, as deemed necessary and on such terms and conditions as may be prescribed. However under sub-section (8), on the same wavelength, it is provided that all employees of a MTI shall have the right to file an appeal in the manner as may be prescribed by rules, against any penalty, termination of their employment or any order in connection with the terms and conditions of CPLA.No.3933/2025,etc -7- their service to the Appellate Tribunal established under Section 16-A of this Act.

In order to deal and decide the appeals preferred under sub-section (7) of section 5 and sub-section (8) of Section 16 of MTI Act and other matters related to or arising from the provisions of this Act, a provision has been incorporated for establishing an Appellate Tribunal by Government in terms of Section 16-A for hearing appeals. Even though, no powers of “Appellate Tribunal” are provided in the parent Act (MTI Act) but such powers are conferred by virtue of Rule 25 of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Medical Teaching Institutions Appellate Tribunal Rules, 2020 framed in exercise of powers conferred under Section 23 of the MTI Act which is reproduced as under:- Powers of the Appellate Tribunal 25. Powers of the Appellate Tribunal. The Appellate Tribunal shall, for the purpose of deciding an appeal, be deemed to be vested with all necessary powers under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act. V of 1908) including the powers of. (a) summoning and enforcing the attendance of any witness and examining him on oath; (b) discovery and production of any document or other material object producible as evidence; (c) accept evidence on affidavit; and (d) requisitioning of any public record from any Court or office and issuing commission for the examination of witnesses and documents or both.

While dismissing both the appeals by dint of impugned judgment, the learned Tribunal observed that appellants (two doctors/petitioners) do not fulfill the five years' experience as Assistant Professor in the relevant discipline in accordance with the minimum standard of PM&DC and declared them ineligible for promotion but at one fell swoop and straight away pronounced that the amended Appendix-8 compiled by Policy Board is against its mandate and declared it ultra vires. What's more, the BoG was also directed to scrutinize the cases of CPLA.No.3933/2025,etc -8- promotions since promulgation of MTI Act, 2015 and the employees who are still in service and had been promoted in any discipline without availability of vacant position shall be reverted back to their original position/grade prior to the benefit of unlawful promotion. Over and above, the learned Tribunal further avowed that the employees who had enjoyed accelerated promotion was ultra vires and the BoG was directed to scrutinize the cases since promulgation of MTI Act and the employees who were promoted under accelerated promotion policy/scheme and still in service would be restored to their original position that existed prior to according benefit to them.

It is well-settled exposition of law that the educational institutions are the best judges of their own rules and regulations because they possess the specialized expertise in the relevant disciplines and traits. It was consistently held that academic, administrative, and disciplinary autonomy of university and professional colleges/institutions must be respected, therefore, the Courts usually abstain from dislocating or disturbing their decisions inter alia relating to the admissions, examinations, rules of promotion, eligibility criteria, disciplinary/unfair means matters. Most often, the Courts left such matters to be decided in the inherent institutional authority having exclusive domain under the doctrine of indoor management but needless to say that all such powers must be within the law and rules, regulating the academia. Interference can only be caused if it disregards the Constitution, its own statute, rules or regulations vis-à-vis the right to education or an unfair procedure violating the principle of natural justice and due process of law or if their decisions are outrageously unreasonable and obstinate.

It is compos mentis that the learned Tribunal under the MTI Act and enabling Rules does not have any suo CPLA.No.3933/2025,etc -9- moto powers to inaugurate proceedings or investigations on its own accord but it has to perform within the sphere of its jurisdiction rather than assuming the role of judicial activism for activating judicial overreach. The judicial power can only be exercised according to the limit of jurisdiction conferred by law as accentuated under Article 175 (2) of the Constitution of Islamic Republic of Pakistan 1973 as an indispensable and elementary tenet that no court shall have any jurisdiction unless it is conferred by the Constitution or under any law. The utmost judicious contrivance for restricting a Court or Tribunal is the law of pleadings. Secundum allegata et probata; the case must be decided according to what is pleaded and proved and should avoid and ignore the issues if raised beyond the boundaries set by the original pleadings. If a Court or Tribunal grounded its judgment on extraneous issues, the resulting order is often considered a nullity or without lawful authority. No doubt the Court sometimes molds a relief to provide substantial and complete justice but even it does not permit to outweigh or overshadow the law and gather up the issues alien to the pleadings from tip to toe. The Court and Tribunal act as neutral arbiters rather than investigators or policy makers or initiating or conducting fishing and roving inquiries. Crossing the bounds of jurisdiction renders the order and decision coram non judice.

Striking down the “Amended Appendix-8” and ordering demotion of all employees since 2015 across the board who were neither party to the proceedings nor at any point of time any effort was made by the learned Tribunal to issue any notice to them for proving right of audience but all such employees were directed to be reverted to their original position that existed prior to according benefit under the promotion policy. The Court and Tribunal has to be within its confines of jurisdiction while deciding the matters. No doubt, under Section 16-A of the MTI Act, the learned Tribunal has been CPLA.No.3933/2025,etc -10- conferred with powers to hear appeals in the matters provided under sub-section (7) of section 5 and sub- section (8) of Section 16 and other matters related to or arising from the provisions of this Act but what it means is, the jurisdiction of the learned Tribunal is delineated to deal and decide the appeal if preferred by any member of the Board against his removal prior to completion of his term of three years or the employees of a Medical Teaching Institution against any penalty, termination of their employment or any order in connection with the terms and conditions of their service.

More to the point, the directions of demotion or reversal of a large number of promoted employees since 2015, not only created serious repercussion and administrative catastrophes but all this was done also without providing any right of audience to numerous reverted employees which gravelly violated the right to fair trial and due process, who one fine morning came to know that are reverted/demoted. The principle of natural justice requires that the delinquent should be afforded a fair opportunity to converge, give explanation and contest it before he is found guilty and condemned. The doctrine of natural justice is destined to safeguard individuals and whatever civil rights, human rights, Constitutional rights or other guaranteed rights under any law are found to be at stake. The principles of natural justice and fair-mindedness are grounded in the philosophy of affording a right of audience before any detrimental action is taken, therefore it is incumbent that all judicial, quasi- judicial and administrative authorities should carry out their powers with a judicious and evenhanded approach to ensure justice according to tenor of law and without any violation of the principle of natural justice. The maxim "no man shall be condemned unheard" is not confined to Courts but extend to all proceedings, by whomsoever held which may affect the person or property or other rights of the parties concerned in CPLA.No.3933/2025,etc -11- the dispute. In order to ensure the elementary and essential principles of fairness as a matter of necessary implication, the person sought to be affected must at least be made aware of the nature of the allegations against him, he should be given a fair opportunity. Reference can be made to the dictum laid down by one of us in the case of Sohail Ahmad Vs. Government of Pakistan through Secretary of Interior Ministry, Islamabad and others (2022 SCMR 1387) & Inspector General of Police, Quetta and another Vs. Fida Muhammad and others (2022 SCMR 1583)].

In the wake of above discussion, the aforesaid Civil Petitions are converted into appeals and allowed. As a consequence thereof, the impugned judgment passed by the learned Tribunal is set aside. Insofar as the claim of promotion of Dr. Yasir Rehman Khattak [CPLA No.922-P/2024] and Dr. Nasreen Kishwar [CPLA No. 923-P/2025] is concerned, they agree to apply afresh for their promotion from BPS-18 to the post of Associate Professor (BPS-19) as according to them, they have completed more than 05 years length of service in BPS-

On submission of fresh applications for promotion, the Dean of Khyber Girls Medical College Pakistan on receiving the applications, immediately forward the dossier for promotion to the IPC for consideration in the next meeting and communicate the decision to both the aforesaid doctors. The C.M.A is disposed of accordingly. Judge Islamabad 18.02.2026 Khalid Approved for reporting. Judge
